cond_0001.intro: The main function of a manufacturing engineer is to apply engineering theory and principles to problems of industrial layout or manufacturing production. A typical manufacturing engineer has the ability to make engineering drawings, and read and interpret blueprints.

Study time, motion, methods, and speed involved in maintenance, production, and other operations to establish standard production rate and improve efficiency.
Interpret engineering drawings, schematic diagrams, or formulas and confer with management or engineering staff to determine quality and reliability standards.
Read worker logs, product processing sheets, and specification sheets, to verify that records adhere to quality assurance specifications.
Aid in planning work assignments in accordance with worker performance, machine capacity, production schedules, and anticipated delays.
Prepare charts, graphs, and diagrams to illustrate workflow, routing, floor layouts, material handling, and machine utilization.
Review installation diagrams and conduct time studies on the shop floor.
Work on Standard Work Instructions (SWI) based on job element sheets (JES) that explain how to build vehicles to operators and are used to hold operators accountable to quality and speed.
Review new model designs with the manufacturing engineering team and determine how to write average installation instructions for components.
Work across areas including cap trim pre-paint, chassis, and as a floater over time.
Launch new models at the plant, including new electric vehicles that differ significantly from current truck builds.

The work involves coordinating with both office and shop floor teams to help improve efficiency and maintain quality standards.
cond_0099.responsibilities:
Work with production and maintenance teams to study time, motion, methods, and speed in order to help establish standard production rates and support efficiency improvements.
Coordinate with management and engineering staff to interpret engineering drawings, schematic diagrams, and formulas, and help determine quality and reliability standards.
Review worker logs, product processing sheets, and specification sheets together with the team to verify that records meet quality assurance requirements.
Support planning of work assignments in alignment with worker performance, machine capacity, production schedules, and anticipated delays.
Prepare charts, graphs, and diagrams in collaboration with the team to illustrate workflow, routing, floor layouts, material handling, and machine utilization.
Partner with manufacturing engineers to review new model designs and help determine installation approaches for components.
Work alongside both office staff and shop floor operators to develop and maintain Standard Work Instructions (SWI) and Job Element Sheets (JES), which guide operators on build quality and pace.
Spend time on the shop floor conducting time studies and supporting the launch of new models, including new electric vehicle platforms that differ significantly from current production.
Coordinate across cap trim, pre-paint, chassis, and floater areas over time.
cond_0099.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, or Manufacturing Engineering
2–4 Years of experience in a related engineering role
Ability to make sketches, engineering drawings, and common computations
Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, schematics, and computer-generated reports
Knowledge of Microsoft products
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with shop floor workers
Willingness to work hands-on and spend time on the production floor
Preferred Requirements:
Prior experience with time studies
Experience with Computer Aided Design (CAD)
Exposure to manual labor or trades work
Analytical and problem-solving ability with attention to detail
Experience with computer applications and software related to the engineering field

cond_0393.intro: The main function of a manufacturing engineer is to apply engineering theory and principles to problems of industrial layout or manufacturing production. A typical manufacturing engineer can make engineering drawings, and read and interpret blueprints. A large part of the role involves staying in regular contact with both engineering staff and floor workers to understand current processes and support production.
cond_0393.responsibilities:
Study time, motion, methods, and speed involved in maintenance, production, and other operations to establish standard production rates and improve efficiency.
Interpret engineering drawings, schematic diagrams, or formulas and actively confer with management or engineering staff to determine quality and reliability standards.
Read worker logs, product processing sheets, and specification sheets to verify that records adhere to quality assurance specifications.
Aid in planning work assignments in accordance with worker performance, machine capacity, production schedules, and anticipated delays.
Prepare charts, graphs, and diagrams to illustrate workflow, routing, floor layouts, material handling, and machine utilization.
Spend regular time on the shop floor conducting time studies and communicating directly with operators to understand current processes.
Review new model designs with manufacturing engineers and initiate discussions to determine how to write standard installation instructions for components.
Develop Standard Work Instructions (SWI) and Job Element Sheets (JES) that explain how to build vehicles to operators, and walk operators through quality and speed expectations.
Work across cap trim pre-paint, chassis, and floater areas over time.
Support the launch of new models, including new electric vehicles that differ significantly from existing truck builds.
cond_0393.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in mechanical, industrial, or manufacturing engineering required.
2–4 Years of experience required.
Degree in Industrial or Mechanical engineering preferred.
Prior work experience with a time study background is very helpful.
Industrial engineering background is a must.
Familiarity with Microsoft products required.
CAD experience is helpful but not required.
Ability to make sketches, engineering drawings, and common computations.
Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, schematics, and computer-generated reports.
Previous experience with computer applications and software related to the engineering field, such as Computer Aided Design (CAD).
Exposure to manual labor and the ability to communicate clearly and comfortably with people working on the floor; willingness to get hands-on.
Creativity, verbal and written communication skills, analytical and problem-solving ability.
Team player and detail oriented.
Some on-the-job training provided for current standards; candidate should have a basic understanding of mechanical or manufacturing engineering.
Will be trained by office staff and spend a significant amount of time with floor staff to build understanding of current processes.
Approximately 50% of the day will be spent on the floor conducting time studies.

The main function of this role is to apply engineering theory and principles to problems of industrial layout or manufacturing production. The role requires the ability to make engineering drawings and read and interpret blueprints.
cond_0475.responsibilities:
Study time, motion, methods, and speed involved in maintenance, production, and other operations to establish standard production rates and improve efficiency.
Interpret engineering drawings, schematic diagrams, or formulas and check with engineering staff to determine quality and reliability standards.
Read worker logs, product processing sheets, and specification sheets to verify that records adhere to quality assurance specifications.
Support planning of work assignments in accordance with worker performance, machine capacity, production schedules, and anticipated delays.
Prepare charts, graphs, and diagrams to illustrate workflow, routing, floor layouts, material handling, and machine utilization.
Review installation diagrams and conduct time studies on the shop floor.
Write standard work instructions (SWI) based on job element sheets (JES) that document how components are installed on new models.
Review new vehicle designs with the manufacturing engineering team to determine installation standards for components.
Support the launch of new vehicle models, including electric vehicles that differ significantly from current production trucks.
Work across cap trim pre-paint, chassis, and floater areas over time.
Spend approximately 30% of the day on focused desk work, 30% on the shop floor, 30% in meetings, and 10% on coordination tasks.
cond_0475.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in mechanical, industrial, or manufacturing engineering
Background in industrial engineering
Ability to make sketches, engineering drawings, and common computations
Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, schematics, and computer-generated reports
Familiarity with Microsoft products
Comfort working hands-on in a manufacturing environment and communicating clearly with production floor staff
Preferred Requirements:
Prior time study experience
Experience with Computer Aided Design (CAD)
Previous exposure to computer applications and software used in engineering
Degree specifically in Industrial or Mechanical Engineering
2–4 Years of relevant work experience
Some on-the-job training for current standards will be provided. Candidates without extensive experience are welcome to apply if they have the right educational background and hands-on aptitude.

People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of manufacturing processes and how production systems fit together.
cond_0634.responsibilities:
Study time, motion, methods, and speed involved in maintenance, production, and other operations to establish standard production rate and improve efficiency.
Interpret engineering drawings, schematic diagrams, or formulas and confer with management or engineering staff to determine quality and reliability standards.
Read worker logs, product processing sheets, and specification sheets, to verify that records adhere to quality assurance specifications.
Aid in planning work assignments in accordance with worker performance, machine capacity, production schedules, and anticipated delays.
Prepare charts, graphs, and diagrams to illustrate workflow, routing, floor layouts, material handling, and machine utilization.
cond_0634.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical, industrial, or manufacturing engineering
Industrial engineering background is a must
Prior work experience with a time study background
Ability to make sketches, engineering drawings and common computations
Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, schematics and computer-generated reports
Knowledge of Microsoft products
Creativity, verbal and written communication skills, analytical and problem solving ability
Team player and detail oriented
Exposure to some manual labor and ability to communicate effectively with people working with their hands
Preferred Requirements
Degree in Industrial or Mechanical engineering
2-4 Years experience
Previous experience with computer applications and software related to engineering field, such as Computer Aided Design (CAD)
CAD experience is not required but could be helpful
Familiarity with standard work instructions (SWI) and job element sheets (JES)

Review worker logs, product processing sheets, and specification sheets together with the team to verify that records adhere to quality assurance specifications.
Support planning of work assignments in accordance with worker performance, machine capacity, production schedules, and anticipated delays.
Prepare charts, graphs, and diagrams in collaboration with the team to illustrate workflow, routing, floor layouts, material handling, and machine utilization.
Spend time on the shop floor working with blue collar staff to understand current processes and conduct time studies.
Coordinate with manufacturing engineers to review new designs and help determine installation standards for components on new models.
Work with the team to develop and maintain standard work instructions (SWI) and job element sheets (JES) that explain how to build vehicles to operators and support accountability to quality and speed.
Support the launch of new models at the plant, including new electric vehicles that differ significantly from existing builds.
Share time across activities: approximately 30% focused desk work, 30% shop floor, 30% meetings, and 10% collaboration.
